'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***[[2021 Kabul school bombing]]
****The death toll from yesterday's school bombing in [[Kabul]] increases to 68 people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghan-school-blast-toll-rises-58-families-bury-victims-2021-05-09/ (Reuters)]
***With multiple electricity pylons near Kabul being destroyed by bomb blasts, electricity supplier Da Afghanistan Breshna Sherkat (DABS) is reporting a shortage of 530 megawatts of power and announced that it will take 20 days to repair the destroyed pylons. Residents are accusing DABS of discrimination during these outages, as the capital's elite had 24-hour electricity. [https://tolonews.com/business-172042 (TOLO News)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**The [[United States Navy]] announces that it has seized a shipment of thousands of weapons in a [[Ship registration|stateless]] [[dhow]] on the [[Arabian Sea]] believed to be en-route to [[Yemen]]. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/05/09/us-navy-seizes-weapons-arabian-sea-486127 (''Politico'')]
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Israel|Israeli Supreme Court]] agrees to delay its ruling on whether [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] residents in [[East Jerusalem]]'s [[Sheikh Jarrah]] neighborhood can be evicted to make way for [[Israeli settlement|Jewish settlers]] to later this month, following a series of violent clashes between Israeli police and Palestinian protesters over this issue. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/may/09/israeli-settlement-ruling-delayed-jerusalem-tensions-palestinians (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Colonial Pipeline cyberattack]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] declares a [[state of emergency#United States|state of emergency]] following  Friday's ransomware cyberattack against [[Colonial Pipeline]], the largest fuel pipeline in the U.S., which transports 2.5 million barrels a day – 45 percent of the [[East Coast of the United States|U.S. East Coast]]'s supply of diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-57050690 (BBC News)]
*A day after appearing on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' and causing [[Dogecoin]]'s value to drop by a third by calling the digital currency a "hustle", [[SpaceX]] CEO [[Elon Musk]] announces that his company will accept the cryptocurrency as payment for a DOGE-1 mission to the Moon. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/dogecoin-spotlight-cryptocurrency-backer-musk-makes-snl-appearance-2021-05-07/ (Reuters)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/09/spacex-accepts-dogecoin-payment-for-doge-1-mission-to-the-moon.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[landslide]] at a clandestine [[gold mine]] in [[Siguiri]], [[Guinea]], kills at least fifteen [[mining industry of Guinea|miners]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-57046636 (BBC News)]
*Rescue operations are underway in southwest [[London]] to help a small whale, believed to be a [[Minke whale|Minke]], stranded in the [[River Thames]], apparently stuck on the [[Richmond Lock and Footbridge|Richmond Lock's]] boat rollers. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-57052331 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] lifts its curfew and some social restrictions, such as requiring a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test]] result to enter certain venues, for those who have been vaccinated or who have recovered from [[COVID-19]]. These people are also no longer required to enter [[quarantine]] unless they have travelled to a high-risk country. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-05-fully-vaccinated-freedoms-germany.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Taoiseach]] [[Micheál Martin]] receives his first dose of the [[AstraZeneca]] [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.irishpost.com/news/taoiseach-micheal-martin-felt-fantastic-after-receiving-first-dose-of-astrazeneca-vaccine-211841 (''The Irish Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] lifts its [[state of emergency]] that had been imposed since October, allowing people to travel freely between [[Autonomous communities of Spain|region]]s for the first time in months. The country's curfew is also lifted. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210509-it-s-like-new-year-s-spain-ends-covid-19-state-of-emergency (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
****[[Laos]] reports its first death from [[COVID-19]]. The patient is a 53-year-old woman who had been receiving treatment at a designated hospital in [[Vientiane]] since April 30. [https://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/269347941/laos-reports-first-covid-19-death (Big News Network)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 26 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 1,683. [https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2021/05/689106/26-covid-19-deaths-highest-daily-figure-pandemic-hit (''New Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] reports a record 2,672 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the cumulative number of patients to 125,906. [https://www.newsfirst.lk/2021/05/09/sri-lanka-reports-record-2672-covid-infections-in-a-single-day/ (Newsfirst)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]], [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****[[Florida]] has reported more than 10,000 cases of the [[Lineage B.1.1.7]], [[Lineage P.1]], and [[Lineage B.1.351]] variants since spring break. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/florida-reports-10000-covid-19-variant-cases-surge/story?id=77553100 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
***[[Tunisia]] enters a seven-day strict [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] during the [[Eid al-Fitr]] holiday, which includes a curfew from 7:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/9/tunisia-begins-week-of-strict-covid-lockdown (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Colorado Springs shooting]]
**Six people are killed by a gunman in a [[mass shooting]] during a birthday party at a residence in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]]. The gunman, who committed suicide at the scene, is believed to have been a boyfriend of one of the victims. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57052452 (BBC News)]
*[[Capital punishment in Egypt]]
**[[Copts|Coptic]] monk Wael Saad Tawadros, better known as Brother Isaiah, is executed over the killing of bishop [[Anba Epiphanius]], the [[abbot]] of the [[Monastery of Saint Macarius the Great]] in [[Wadi El Natrun]], in 2018. [https://www.macaubusiness.com/egypt-hangs-coptic-monk-for-killing-of-abbot-family/ (''Macau Business'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Colombian protests]]
**[[Claudia Blum]], the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Colombia, resigns from her post amidst the ongoing [[2021 Colombian protests|anti-government protests]] that have killed at least 26 people. [https://www.semana.com/nacion/articulo/se-va-del-cargo-la-canciller-claudia-blum/202104/ (Semana)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Environmental issues in Kyrgyzstan]]
**A court in [[Kyrgyzstan]] fines a company owned by [[Centerra Gold]] 261.7 billion [[Kyrgyz som|soms]] for environmental pollution at the [[Kumtor Gold Mine]]. [https://www.brecorder.com/news/40091431/kyrgyz-court-fines-canadian-gold-miner-25bn-euros (Business Recorder)]
*The China Manned Space Engineering Office says that remnants of the Chinese [[Long March 5|Long March-5B Y2]] rocket made an uncontrolled re-entry into [[Earth]]'s atmosphere into the [[Indian Ocean]], just west of the [[Maldives]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/05/08/app-international-edition/china-space-debris-long-march-rocket-reentry-scn/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/08/science/china-rocket-reentry-falling-long-march-5b.html (''The New York Times'')]
*South Korea reports that it now holds the world's largest number of [[Essential patent|standard-essential patents]] followed by the [[United States]], [[Finland]], and [[Japan]]. Standard-essential patents refer to major technologies that are vital in producing standardized products and that must be verified by standards organizations.  [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20210509001100320?section=news (Yonhap)]
